newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: GIPPSLAND BY-ELECTION RESULT

The result of Victoria's Gippsland West by-election won't be known for several days. But a swing against the Kennett Government in weekend polls could see the traditionally safe Liberal seat become one of the party's most marginal.
Independent Susan Davies has increased her lead and at the end of postal and pre-ballot vote counting yesterday, she was 328 votes ahead of Liberal Matthew Coleman on a two-candidate preferred basis.
SENATOR WORRIED ABOUT WASTE DUMPING IN REEF
A North Queensland Senator says it is outrageous the Environment Minister is proposing to allow defence vessels to dump waste in Barrier Reef waters during exercises next month.

Senator Margaret Reynolds says Minister Robert Hill, will be introducing amendment legislation to Federal Parliament this week to allow U.S. and Australian ships to discharge waste off Shoalwater Bay.
She's called on all Queensland Senators and Federal members to force a review, before the exercises, called Operation Tandum Thrust, in April.
FLOODING PROBLEMS IN TWO STATES
Flooding in inland Queensland and north west New South Wales is still causing problems for property owners, businesses and motorists.

The Warrego River in Western Queensland is at nearly six and a half metres and still rising. Five homes in Charleville were innundated yesterday and a number of roads in the state's southwest have been cut.
Authorities are watching the river further upstream in the Warrego catchment at Augathella and Tambo after more rain overnight.
In the border area, the Cunningham Highway between the towns of Goondiwindi and Inglewood has been closed to cars because of flooding.

In north western New South Wales, dozens of property owners in the Namoi Valley remain isolated as floodwaters continue to move through the area. The town of Wee Waa was also isolated for most of the weekend, but the main road to Narrabri has now been re-opened. The town itself is protected by levees.
State Emergency Service units now have 10 floodboats on standby in case of emergency, but say there've been no problems. - - - -
BOND BACK IN COURT TODAY
Former tycoon, Alan Bond, is due to appear in the Supreme Court in Perth today for submissions on what sentence he should receive for his part in the nation's biggest case of corporate fraud.

In December, Bond pleaded guilty to two charges of failing to act honestly as a company director. The charges related to the transfer of more than one billion dollars from the company, Bell Resources, to the Bond Corporation in the late 1980s.
Bond's guilty plea came after a deal with the prosecution in which a string of more serious charges were dropped.
Whatever sentence Bond receives, it'll be added to the three year term he's already serving for an art fraud conviction - he's served more than four months of that sentence.
The sentencing hearing on these latest charges is expected to last a few days.
CIVIL LIBERTIES UNHAPPY WITH GOVERNMENT ON HUMAN RIGHTS
The Council for Civil Liberties has called on the Federal Government to drop its objections to a human rights clause in a trade agreement with the European Union.
The Council's National President, Terry O'Gorman, says the Government's stance will damage important trade links between Australia and the E-U and its international standing on human rights.
He says some observers believe Australia failed to win a seat on the United Nations Security Council last year because of its appalling human rights record in relation to Aborigines.
PRISONS COMMISSIONER SAYS NO TO NEEDLE PROGRAM

New South Wales Corrective Service Commissioner, Leo Keliher says needle exchage programs in jails would put prison staff at risk. This follows calls by doctors who want clean needles made available to stop the spread of Hebatitis-C among prisoners.
Research published in the Medical Journal of Australia reveals almost 40 per cent of inmates entering the state's jails become infected with the disease.
Doctor Keliher says it's ludicrous to call for a needle exchange program, because of dangers to staff.
He says one prison officer has already contracted AIDS after a deliberate needle stick attack in a jail.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
